import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 236

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/236](https://www.erdosproblems.com/236)
-/

open Filter Asymptotics

namespace Erdos236

/--
$f(n)$ counts the number of solutions to $n=p+2^k$ for prime $p$ and $k\geq 0$.
-/
def f (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ((List.range (Nat.log2 n + 1)).filter (fun k => Nat.Prime (n - 2^k))).length

/--
Let $f(n)$ count the number of solutions to $n=p+2^k$ for prime $p$ and $k\geq 0$. Show that $f(n)=o(\log n)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_236: (fun n => (f n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n => Real.log (n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos236

reformulations.difference: Counts filtered exponents through Nat.log2 n using natural subtraction, rather than explicitly counting pairs (p,k) satisfying n = p + 2^k.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every representation has 2^k ≤ n and hence k ≤ Nat.log2 n. Conversely, primality of n - 2^k implies this difference is at least 2, so subtraction cannot have truncated and n = (n - 2^k) + 2^k. Each exponent determines exactly one prime summand, and List.range contains no duplicates. At n = 0 both counts vanish. In scratch.lean, proved for every n that f n equals the cardinality of {pk : ℕ × ℕ | pk.1.Prime ∧ n = pk.1 + 2^pk.2}, and proved equivalence of the resulting little-o statements.

sources_consulted: Local Lean/Mathlib sources for Nat.log2, Nat.Prime, List.range/filter, Filter.atTop, Asymptotics.IsLittleO, and Real.log.
